# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### VolumeReadBytes alarm firing on vol-0123456789abcdef0
**Description:** CloudWatch alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes ([redacted ARN]) moved to ALARM at 2026-11-23T18:11:18Z. Its last 3 datapoints (18:08–18:10, Sum per 60s) were ~7.869e9 bytes, above the 6.0e9 threshold. The alarm has no actions configured.
**Time:** 2026-11-23T18:08:00Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: gp3 volume pinned at its 125 MiB/s provisioned throughput cap
**Description:** Volume vol-0123456789abcdef0 (gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s, unchanged gp3 defaults since 2026-11-11) on i-1234567890abcdef0_5 (c6i.xlarge, account 012345678901_1, us-east-1) has served reads at exactly 125.07 MiB/s every minute from 18:08Z to 19:33Z, with 0 writes. The job reads in 256 KiB requests, so the cap allows only ~500 IOPS (~17% of 3000), which is why IOPS looks normal. Queue depth ~1.5 and ~3 ms latency show requests held back by bandwidth, not a slow device. The 6e9 bytes/min alarm threshold (~95 MiB/s) is crossed at ~7.87e9 bytes/min, so example-b-gp3-read-bytes went to ALARM at 18:11:18Z. Instance bandwidth (~132.9 of ~149 MiB/s sustained, burst balance 99%) and CPU (~1%) are not the limit yet.
**Cascades to:** symptom-ebs-read-bytes-alarm

#### Supporting Observations
- **Read throughput flat at 125 MiB/s, IOPS ~500:** From 18:08 to 19:33 UTC, reads on vol-0123456789abcdef0 hold at 125.07 MiB/s every minute, using 256 KiB requests at ~500 IOPS. The workload is read-only (0 writes). Queue length is ~1.5 and average read latency is ~3 ms, with brief spikes to ~7.5 ms. VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeIOPSExceededCheck returned no datapoints.
- **gp3 volume at baseline 3000 IOPS / 125 MiB/s on a non-EBS-optimized c6i.xlarge:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 (example-b-gp3-throughput) is a 20 GiB gp3 volume provisioned at 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s, attached as /dev/sdg to i-1234567890abcdef0_5 (c6i.xlarge, us-east-1a, EbsOptimized=false, launched 2026-11-23T18:05:10Z). The instance also has 3 other volumes attached. The observed ~7.87e9 bytes/min works out to ~131 MB/s, which is ≈125 MiB/s, matching the volume's provisioned throughput ceiling.
- **Instance EBS headroom intact (EBSByteBalance% 99%):** EBSByteBalance% and EBSIOBalance% stayed at 99% and CPU ~1%. Instance EBS traffic ~132.9 MiB/s: 125 MiB/s on /dev/sdg plus ~7.8 MiB/s on io2 vol-1234567890abcdef0_4 (/dev/sdf). The root volume vol-1234567890abcdef0_20 does ~0.01 MiB/s and vol-1234567890abcdef0_16 (/dev/sdi) is idle, so ~141 MiB/s of headroom remains for /dev/sdg against the c6i.xlarge baseline of 156.25 MB/s (~149 MiB/s).
- **No volume modifications or recent config changes:** DescribeVolumesModifications returned NotFound: the volume has never been modified and is still on the gp3 defaults. CloudTrail shows no events on vol-0123456789abcdef0 since Nov 22. The only events on i-1234567890abcdef0_5 since 17:00 are AssumeRole calls at 18:05:12 (matching the 18:05:10 launch) and at 18:47:29.
- **Recurring 125 MiB/s read plateau since Nov 11:** Hourly VolumeReadBytes on vol-0123456789abcdef0 shows the same ~7.87e9 bytes/min peak minute in many hours: Nov 11 00:00–01:00 and 15:00, and Nov 23 from 07:00 on. The hourly average held at 125.07 MiB/s from 08:00 to 12:00 on Nov 23, and the activity resumed at 16:00 and 18:00. Read jobs consistently saturate the volume at the same throughput.

#### Gaps
- **Job's actual throughput need unknown:** No iostat or job logs from inside i-1234567890abcdef0_5 were available, so the throughput the batch job actually wants could not be measured. Size the new volume throughput from that data if possible.
- **Trigger of the recent slowdown not confirmed:** The cap has been hit continuously since 18:08Z, and earlier runs (today and 2026-11-11) also sat at 125 MiB/s. That points to the job reading more data or entering a read-heavy phase, not a volume change, but AWS data could not confirm which.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
Raise gp3 volume vol-0123456789abcdef0 throughput from 125 to 250 MiB/s online (keep 3000 IOPS); optionally resize i-1234567890abcdef0_5 to c6i.2xlarge in a maintenance window; retune alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes.

## Reasoning
The job reads at exactly the 125 MiB/s cap with ~500 of 3000 IOPS used and ~1% CPU, so throughput is the only bottleneck. 3000 IOPS supports up to 750 MiB/s, and the change applies with no detach or reboot. 250 MiB/s doubles the cap without overshooting the job's unknown demand. The c6i.xlarge EBS baseline (~149 MiB/s, shared by all four volumes) caps sustained gains at ~141 MiB/s once burst credits run out, so holding 250 MiB/s for a multi-hour job needs c6i.2xlarge (~298 MiB/s baseline). The alarm threshold (~95 MiB/s) sits below the old cap and will keep firing unless retuned.

### Requirements

#### 1. Make the new volume throughput (and instance type, if changed) part of the infrastructure definition.
**Description:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 has run on gp3 defaults (125 MiB/s) since 2026-11-11 and every job run hits that cap. Wherever this volume and instance are defined (CloudFormation, CDK, Terraform or launch templates for Project=example, Scenario=b), set gp3 Throughput to the proven value (250 MiB/s or higher) with Iops 3000, and InstanceType c6i.2xlarge if resized. Ensure the provisioned throughput fits the instance EBS baseline after counting other attached volumes.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A new deployment creates the volume with Throughput >= 250 MiB/s and Iops >= 3000.
- A new deployment does not revert the manual change.
- The instance type's EBS baseline is at least the sum of the attached volumes' sustained throughput.

#### 2. Replace the fixed-bytes alarm with a saturation alarm.
**Description:** Redefine example-b-gp3-read-bytes as a saturation alarm: throughput in MiB/s at or above 95% of provisioned throughput for a sustained period. Optionally add an alarm on the instance's EBSByteBalance% below 20%.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- The alarm stays OK during normal job runs that don't reach the cap.
- The alarm fires within 15 minutes when throughput sits at 95% or more of the provisioned value.
- An EBSByteBalance% alarm exists for i-1234567890abcdef0_5.
